title: Undo moves: add minus numbers
goal: Add minus numbers on the line, use N1–N5, and give the reasons in a short proof.
generalHint: Put the start number on the line. A plus number moves to the right. A minus number moves to the left.

screens.label: RECALL
screens.title: Where is minus 3?

answer.correctWhy: Minus 3 is 3 units to the left of 0.

mistakes.reply: That is plus 3. Minus numbers are on the other side of 0. Which side is that?

hints: Minus numbers are on the left of 0.
screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: PUZZLE
screens.title: It is 10° outside. Tonight the temperature decreases by 15°.
screens.prompt: Do not calculate yet. Guess where the temperature stops.

sameSide.correctWhy: The first 10° take the temperature to 0°. The last 5° take it below zero.

otherSide.correctWhy: The temperature decreases by more than 10°, so it goes past 0°. 10 − 15 = −5.

screens.caption: Drag the orange ring, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Adding a minus number
screens.prompt: Start at 3. To add $-5$, make 5 hops to the left. Drag the ring 5 hops.

answer.correctWhy: Start at 3 and make 5 hops to the left. You pass 0 after 3 hops, then go 2 more.

mistakes.reply: That is 3 + 5. Adding −5 means a move to the left. Try the hops again.
You stopped at plus 2. Count the hops again: the fifth hop goes past 0.

screens.tryTask: Now start at −3 and add +3. Where do you land? Why?
hints: A minus number moves to the left.

steps.text: Make one hop to the left for each unit of 5.

answer.correctWhy: 4 hops to the left of 2 is −2.

screens.caption: Make all 5 hops, then check.

screens.label: EXPLORE
screens.title: Order does not change the sum
screens.prompt: Look at the two paths. $3 + 5$ and $5 + 3$ use different hops. Lang assumes two rules about this. He also writes $a - b$ for $a + (-b)$.

followUp.question: Does $(-2 + 5) + 4$ stop at the same point as $-2 + (5 + 4)$?

options.label: No, they stop at different points
options.reply: Calculate the two: (−2 + 5) + 4 = 3 + 4, and −2 + (5 + 4) = −2 + 9. Compare the results.

feedback.correctWhy: The grouping does not change the sum. This is associativity. Lang assumes it, with commutativity.

hints: Calculate the brackets first on each side.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Every number has an undo
screens.prompt: Make 3 hops right, then 3 hops left. You return to 0. Lang writes this as a rule.

note.label: WORDS MATTER
note.text: Say −a as “minus a”, not “negative a”. If a = −3, then −a = 3, which is positive.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Two mirrors bring you back
screens.prompt: Minus moves a number to its mirror point across 0. Do this two times, and you are back at the start. This is N4: $-(-a) = a$.

answer.correctWhy: The first minus gives −4. The second minus mirrors −4 back to 4.

mistakes.reply: That is one mirror. There are two minus signs. Mirror −4 again.

hints: Mirror 4 across 0. Then mirror the result again.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Each number has one undo
screens.prompt: If $a + b = 0$, then $b$ must be $-a$. Lang calls this N3. Give the reason for each step.

wrongReasonReplies.comm-add: Commutativity changes the order of two terms. What changed in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-add: Associativity changes the brackets. What changed in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.N1: N1 removes a 0 that is added. Is there a 0 to remove in this line?
wrongReasonReplies.N2: N2 changes a + (−a) into 0. Look for a number next to its minus.
wrongReasonReplies.add-both: This step adds a new term to both sides. Did this line add a term?

feedback.correctWhy: You used only N1, N2 and one move that keeps the balance. So the undo of a number is unique.

screens.caption: Tap a rule to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Minus of a sum
screens.prompt: Prove N5: $-(a + b) = -a - b$. Show that $-a - b$ undoes $a + b$. Then use N3.

wrongReasonReplies.comm-add: Commutativity changes the order of terms. Did the order change, or only the brackets?
wrongReasonReplies.assoc-add: Associativity changes the brackets. Did the brackets change, or the order?
wrongReasonReplies.N3: N3 is the last step: a sum is 0, so one term is minus the other. Is the sum 0 yet?
wrongReasonReplies.N4: N4 removes two minus signs. Is there −(−a) in this line?

feedback.correctWhy: The sum is 0, so N3 gives −a − b = −(a + b). Lang uses this proof.

screens.caption: Tap a rule to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: PROVE IT
screens.title: Two minus numbers make a minus sum
screens.prompt: Lang assumes that a sum of positive integers is positive. Use this to prove: if $a$ and $b$ are negative, then $a + b$ is negative.

lines.reasonLabel: minus a positive number is negative

steps.label: minus a positive number is negative

wrongReasonReplies.N4: N4 removes two minus signs. This line has a minus in front of a sum.
wrongReasonReplies.N5: N5 changes −(a + b) into −a − b. Read this line from right to left.
wrongReasonReplies.pos-sum: This rule is about a sum of positive numbers. Which numbers here are positive?
wrongReasonReplies.comm-add: The order of the terms did not change.

feedback.correctWhy: You proved a new rule from one rule that Lang assumes and one that you proved.

screens.caption: Tap a rule to fill the orange slot.

screens.label: NAME IT
screens.title: Keep the balance
screens.prompt: If $a + b = c$, then $a = c - b$. Add $-b$ to both sides. Remove 3 cubes from each pan to find $x$.

answer.correctWhy: x + 3 = 5, so x = 5 − 3 = 2. The balance stays level because you removed 3 from both pans.

mistakes.reply: That is 5 + 3. To keep the balance, remove 3 from both pans. Do not add.

hints: Remove the same number of cubes from each pan.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 1 OF 3
screens.title: Your turn

answer.correctWhy: 9 hops to the left of 7: 7 hops take you to 0, then 2 more.

mistakes.reply: That is 7 + 9. A minus number moves to the left. Which direction did you hop?
The size is correct, but the sign is not. You go past 0. Which side of 0 do you stop on?

hints: Go to 0 first. How many hops are left?

answer.correctWhy: 4 hops take you to 0, then 2 more to the left.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 2 OF 3
screens.title: Your turn
screens.prompt: Be careful when you take minus of a sum with minus signs inside.

mistakes.reply: −6 + 8 is 2. That is correct. A minus sign is still outside the brackets. What is minus 2?
The outer minus changes every sign inside. What are −(−6) and −(8)?
Calculate inside the brackets first: −6 + 8. Then apply the outer minus.

hints: Then apply the minus outside: minus 2 is −2.

screens.label: PRACTICE · 3 OF 3
screens.title: Solve
screens.prompt: Find the missing number in each problem.

mistakes.reply: Do a check: −3 − 7 = −10, not 4. Which y makes −3 − y equal to 4?
Do a check: −3 − 1 = −4, not 4. Add 3 to both sides first: −y = 7.

parts.prompt: An account shows −20. After a deposit, the account shows 35. Find the deposit.

mistakes.reply: That is 35 − 20. The account starts below 0. How far is it from −20 to 35?

hints: Use the rule from the balance: if a + b = c, then a = c − b.

screens.label: LESSON 1.2 COMPLETE
screens.title: You can undo any number.
screens.prompt: You use these rules in all later chapters:

trap.question: True or false: −a is always a negative number.

options.label: True
options.reply: Put in a = −3. Then −a = −(−3) = 3, which is positive.

feedback.correctWhy: If a is negative, then −a is positive. This is why Lang says “minus a”.

screens.caption: Saved to your rule book.
